properties.rationale:
ACCEPTED WHILE PLANNED, AND NOW DATED — Anthony's call 2026-07-31, taken with the other three of its kind as one judgement.

The gap's literal question — "how will you confirm it?" — is ALREADY ANSWERED: ver:gap-carries-a-reading is written and sits at `planned`, and it pins the CONTRACT rather than the judgement. What the gap actually reports is that the check has never RUN, which is simply true of anything unbuilt. That is a fact about sequencing, not a hole in the design.

WHY ACCEPT RATHER THAN LEAVE OPEN: these four were the only notes on the gate, so every release cut printed "5 notes" with no way to tell signal from permanent background — which is how a gate stops being read. When the capability is built and its check passes, the gap disappears on its own.

*** CORRECTION, MADE THE SAME DAY, LEFT ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN EDITED AWAY. *** This rationale originally claimed that `cap:review-expires-on-content` "means rewording the capability expires this review and brings it back for a fresh look". THAT IS FALSE. That capability is PLANNED, NOT BUILT. Expiry is keyed on the gap id, which hashes the affected node IDS — so a review expires when the affected SET changes membership and NEVER when the affected nodes change CONTENT. This review therefore does NOT self-expire. If the capability is reworded, someone must revisit this judgement BY HAND.

*** AND IT WAS PROVEN LIVE, WITHIN THE HOUR, ON THIS VERY ACKNOWLEDGEMENT. *** Later in the same session Anthony asked for the recommendation-with-options behaviour to be cemented, and cap:gap-carries-a-reading was substantially rewritten: renamed, given three shape obligations and a language rule, and its check rewritten with two new negative assertions. THIS ACKNOWLEDGEMENT CARRIED ACROSS UNCHANGED and went on suppressing the gap, with reviewed_gaps now rendering the OLD judgement against the NEW text. That is precisely the failure cap:review-expires-on-content exists to fix — in its own words, "a review outliving the wording it reviewed is worse than no review, because it reads as a human having agreed to something they never saw" — reproduced by the very sentence asserting it could not happen.

SO THIS ONE NEEDS A FRESH LOOK AND IS FLAGGED AS SUCH: Anthony judged a capability that said "a question comes with what the agent would do". It now also demands selectable options, a marked recommendation, a consequence on every option, and answering in the user's own language. The judgement (accept while planned, scheduled v0.21.0) plausibly still holds, but it is HIS to re-affirm, not mine to assume.

WHY IT IS SCHEDULED AND NOT MERELY ACCEPTED: acceptance alone was the trap. All four were scheduled against NOTHING, so quieting them would have relied on someone remembering. Now SCHEDULED_FOR rel:v0210 as `expected`, so arrival_delta asks at v0.21.0 regardless. Deliberately `expected` rather than `required`: a plan, not an obligation whose miss is a computed violation.

DELIBERATELY NOT IN v0.20.0, which Anthony scoped to cap:changelog-view alone.
